name: Michael Bidwill

views.text: This is a league about wins and losses, and the record speaks for itself.
I talk it through with my general manager before any firing.
A general manager who builds the roster gets another coach before he gets replaced.
I like young, energetic first-time head coaches.
A franchise record for losses cannot stand.
The quarterback has to be the center of the next coach's plan.

signatures: praises a fired coach in glowing terms
keeps his general manager through coaching changes
want: A sustained winner in Arizona after years of short coaching cycles (medium).
fear: Another three-year cycle that ends in a firing (medium).
voice: Upbeat and complimentary even in bad news, then blunt about results. Former prosecutor's cadence: short declarative sentences.

evidence.summary: Arizona fired Jonathan Gannon after a 3-14 season (15-36 over three years); Bidwill and GM Monti Ossenfort talked before informing him, and Ossenfort kept his job.
Bidwill praised Gannon as a smart, motivated coach but said the league is about wins and losses.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
